title: Countable and uncountable 1
subtitle: a banana / rice
summary: Learn the difference between countable nouns (a banana, two bananas) and uncountable nouns (rice, music), and which words go with each.

left.label: Countable: banana
left.text: A countable noun can be singular (**banana**) or plural (**bananas**). We can use numbers with it: one banana, two bananas.

right.label: Uncountable: rice
right.text: An uncountable noun has only one form (**rice**). There is no plural, and we cannot use numbers with it - not ~~one rice~~, ~~two rices~~.

lesson.heading: Some typical examples
rows: It wasn't your fault. It was **an accident**.
It wasn't your fault. It was bad **luck**.
There are no **batteries** in the radio.
There is no **electricity** in this house.

lesson.heading: a/an with countable nouns
lesson.text: You can use **a/an** with singular countable nouns: *a beach, a student, an umbrella*. You cannot use a singular countable noun alone, without a/the/my etc.

examples.note: plural countable nouns can be used alone: = bananas in general

lesson.heading: No a/an with uncountable nouns
lesson.text: We do not use **a/an** with uncountable nouns - not ~~a sand~~, ~~a music~~, ~~a rice~~. But you can often use **a ... of**: *a bowl of rice, a packet of rice, a grain of rice*. Uncountable nouns can be used alone, without the/my/some.

lesson.heading: Words that go with each type

left.label: Plural countable
examples: I have **a few things** to do.

right.label: Uncountable
examples: I have **a little work** to do.

lesson.text: Quick test: if you can say *two ...s*, the noun is countable and needs a/an in the singular. If you cannot, it is uncountable and takes no a/an and no plural.

exercises.statement: Joe goes everywhere by bike. He doesn't have car.
exercises.explanation: He doesn't have a car. Car is a singular countable noun, so it needs a/an.

exercises.statement: Helen was listening to music when I arrived.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Music is uncountable, so it is used alone without a/an.

exercises.prompt: My brother works for ___ insurance company.
exercises.explanation: Company is a singular countable noun, and insurance begins with a vowel sound: an insurance company.

exercises.statement: I like your suggestion. It's interesting idea.
exercises.explanation: It's an interesting idea. Idea is countable and singular, so it needs an.

exercises.prompt: I couldn't get into the house. I didn't have ___.
exercises.explanation: Key is countable, so the singular needs a.

exercises.prompt: Match each beginning with the noun that completes it correctly.

exercises.explanation: Biscuit is a singular countable noun: a biscuit.

exercises.prompt: Our lives would be very difficult without ___.
exercises.explanation: Electricity is uncountable, so it is used alone.

exercises.prompt: I had ___ for a job yesterday. It went quite well.
exercises.explanation: Interview is countable and begins with a vowel sound: an interview.

exercises.prompt: Outside the cinema there was ___ of people waiting to see the film.
exercises.explanation: Queue is a singular countable noun: a queue of people.

exercises.prompt: Paul always wants things quickly. He doesn't have much ___.
exercises.explanation: Patience is uncountable - that is also why we say much, not many.

exercises.prompt: Is each noun countable or uncountable?
